title: Lumberjack Breakfast Platter
subtitle: Pancakes, eggs, bacon, sausage, and hash browns for a hungry crew.
description: Eggs, bacon, sausage, pancakes, and hash browns on one big platter. The lumberjack spread for crews with big appetites after a long night.

ingredients.name: pancake mix
ingredients.notes: prepared per package for 24 silver-dollar cakes

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Lumberjack Breakfast Platter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook bacon and sausage
steps.instruction: Lay bacon on sheet pans and roast at 400°F until crisp, about 15 minutes. Sear sausage links in a skillet over medium until browned and internal temperature reaches 160°F, about 12 minutes. Hold warm tented with foil.

steps.title: Crisp hash browns
steps.instruction: Spread hash browns on a lightly oiled griddle in a thin layer. Cook undisturbed 4 minutes for crust, then flip sections and cook until golden. Season with salt and pepper; hold warm.

steps.title: Mix and griddle pancakes
steps.instruction: Prepare pancake batter per package using milk and melted butter. Griddle silver-dollar pancakes over medium until bubbles form and edges set, flip, and cook until centers reach 190°F and bottoms are golden.

steps.title: Cook eggs to order
steps.instruction: Fry or scramble eggs in butter over medium heat until whites are fully set (165°F) for fried, or until scrambled curds are moist but not wet. Season each batch with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Lumberjack Breakfast Platter onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Platter and serve
steps.instruction: Arrange pancakes, bacon, sausage, hash browns, and eggs on warm platters with syrup and butter at the line. Serve family-style so the crew builds their own lumberjack plate.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Lumberjack Breakfast Platter — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Run oven bacon and griddle hash in parallel while one cook manages pancake batter.
Hold meats tented with foil on a warm tray—never cover bacon tightly or it steams soft.
Cook eggs last to order so yolks stay runny for crew who want dippers for hash.
cleanupNotes: Drain bacon fat from sheet pans into a heat-safe container once cooled.
Scrape griddle while still warm with a bench scraper before pancake batter dries on.
leftovers: Reheat pancakes on a griddle 2 minutes per side; microwave makes them rubbery.
Chop leftover meats and potatoes into a next-day breakfast burrito filling with eggs.
